questions.text: Which products should I push in my next campaign?
checks: recall of push_candidates >= 2/3
does not recommend do_not_push_for_margin products as the main push
cites margin AND rating AND volume evidence
numbers match recomputed values
recommendation cites a marketing principle from the KB

questions.text: Why are customers unhappy with the Backpacks category?
checks: names zipper failures as the main theme
isolates product P10 (Alder Daypack 20L)
identifies that it started around August 2025
does not blame delivery or the whole category
numbers match

questions.text: Who are my best customers and how do I keep them?
checks: top-10% share of revenue within +/-3 pts
notes they use fewer discounts
identifies jackets as their top category
retention actions are NOT blanket discounts
excludes internal test customers

questions.text: What message should I use to sell the Trail Shell Jacket?
checks: leads with lightweight / packable (customer language)
does not use the banned claim 'waterproof'
mentions light-rain handling only as water resistance
addresses the pockets objection or avoids contradicting it
grounded in review evidence + brand tone

questions.text: Why did revenue drop in March?
checks: compares per-day revenue (Feb has 28 days)
names the Trail Shell Jacket stockout as the primary cause
names the paid-social acquisition cut as secondary
does not attribute it to seasonality or lower demand
excludes cancelled/returned/test orders

questions.text: Which customers are about to churn, and what should I send them?
checks: at-risk list precision and recall >= 0.8 vs gold set (or equivalent stated rule)
rule is explicit (repeat buyer + overdue vs own gap)
win-back offer is matched to past categories
does not default to a deep discount

questions.text: Which acquisition channel brings the best customers, and should I move budget?
checks: restricts CAC and value to 2025 signups
uses a fair window (first 90 days) or flags censoring
identifies paid_social as lowest value and repeat rate
recommends shifting budget away from paid_social toward efficient channels with caveats
numbers match

questions.text: Did my July sale actually work?
checks: reports revenue lift AND gross-profit lift separately
accounts for discount cost
checks the post-sale dip
notes most window orders came from existing customers
does not declare success on revenue alone

questions.text: What should I bundle or cross-sell?
checks: uses lift (not raw popularity)
finds the three planted pairs
does not recommend a pair with lift < 1 as a bundle
gives a concrete bundle or cross-sell action

questions.text: How do my prices compare with my competitors?
checks: says competitor price data is not available
does not invent competitor prices
may offer own price positioning or what data to collect
no fabricated citations
